model.name: Occurrence / Event
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral backbone for recording that a discrete thing happened in the world — what occurred, when, where, who or what took part, on what evidence, with what certainty, and how it relates to other occurrences — so that every specialised event model reuses one shape for time, place, participation, causality and record correction.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the record of an individuated occurrence: its identity and boundary, its type, its factual and record status, its temporal position and extent (including event time versus observation and ingestion time, temporal reference frames and stated uncertainty), its spatial or virtual setting, the participation of parties and objects and the entities used or generated, its part-whole and causal relations to other occurrences, the sources and evidence on which it is asserted, and the governance of the record (stewardship, disclosure, correction, retention, alignment and exchange). It is deliberately storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of these semantics, not the semantics.
in_scope: Individuation and identity of a single occurrence, including deduplication keys and identifier supersession
Occurrence typing against governed code lists and mapping to external event vocabularies
Factual and record status, including negative assertions (it did not happen) and in-error records
Temporal position and extent as instants, intervals, durations and open-ended spans, with an explicit temporal reference frame
Separation of event time, phenomenon time, observation/result time, record/ingestion time and correction declaration time
Stated temporal precision, approximation and uncertainty, including unspecified components
Place and setting statements that reference, but do not define, external place identities; geometry with a declared CRS
Participation of parties and objects, the capacity or role in which each took part, and delegation of responsibility for participation
Entities used, generated, transformed or invalidated by the occurrence, and the quantities involved
Part-whole, series and episode aggregation of occurrences
Asserted causal and influence links between occurrences, with asserter and confidence
Source records, reporting chains, evidence artifacts and their integrity and custody
Append-only correction, retraction and supersession of occurrence records
Stewardship, participant-level disclosure control, retention classes and disposition
Alignment to external standards and projection into exchange envelopes
out_of_scope: Intent, deliberation, motive and moral or legal responsibility of an actor — these specialise the occurrence in the Act model
Reciprocity and mutual-participation semantics — these specialise the occurrence in the Encounter model
Identity, attributes and lifecycle of participating persons, organisations and assets
Identity, naming, addressing and gazetteer resolution of places
Result values, units, scales and measurement uncertainty of observations
Planned, requested or scheduled future actions and their fulfilment workflow
Type-level recurring patterns and phenomena as distinct from their individual instances
State conditions that hold over an interval without being a discrete happening
Incident triage, escalation and response workflow
Transport bindings, wire formats, serialization and query-language syntax
System audit trails of operations performed on the record store
Business process and workflow definitions that occurrences might conform to

boundary_notes.distinction: PROV-O separates mere occurrence from agent responsibility (prov:wasAssociatedWith, prov:Association) and CIDOC CRM separates E5 Event from E7 Activity, defined as actions intentionally carried out by an actor; intent and responsibility therefore belong to the Act model while this model records only that parties participated and in what capacity.

This model records participation as a set of one-sided involvements; reciprocal or mutual participation between two or more parties, and the obligations arising from it, are added by the Encounter specialisation.

SOSA treats an Observation as an act that occurs and therefore as an occurrence, but the observable property, procedure, sensor and result value belong to the measurement model; this model retains only the linkage and the phenomenonTime/resultTime distinction.

GeoSPARQL separates geo:Feature (the identified real-world thing) from geo:Geometry (its spatial representation); this model carries the geometry and the granularity of a place statement but references Feature identity externally.

The HL7 FHIR workflow patterns distinguish Event (an activity that has taken place or is ongoing) from Request (a desired future action); scheduled-but-not-yet-occurred items are not occurrences here, which is why schema.org eventStatus values such as EventScheduled are treated as schedule state, not factual status.
A recurring pattern is a type-level construct; this model records individual instances and may reference the series they instantiate, but does not define the pattern itself.

OWL-Time distinguishes a temporal entity from what holds during it; states that persist over an interval are situations, while this model records the discrete happenings that open, advance and close them.

CloudEvents defines an occurrence as the statement of fact and the event as the data record expressing it with context; the envelope attributes id, source, type and time are a projection of this model's identity, typing and event-time semantics, not additional semantics.

Operations performed on the occurrence store are audited elsewhere; what stays here is the provenance of the assertion itself — who reported it, when it was recorded and by what declaration it was corrected.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of prov:Activity (something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities), prov:Entity, prov:Agent, startedAtTime/endedAtTime, wasAssociatedWith, wasAttributedTo, wasInformedBy, wasDerivedFrom, the qualified Association/Usage/Generation/Communication pattern and prov:atLocation.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL (OWL-Time)
sources.version_or_date: W3C Recommendation 19 October 2017; Candidate Recommendation Draft 15 November 2022
sources.relevance: TemporalEntity with the two subclasses Instant and Interval, hasBeginning/hasEnd/hasTemporalDuration, Allen interval relations, DateTimeDescription and TimePosition, and the hasTRS property that makes the temporal reference system explicit for non-Gregorian, ordinal and geologic scales.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.version_or_date: RFC 3339, July 2002, Proposed Standard (updated by RFC 9557)
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar requiring seconds and a time-offset of 'Z' or a numeric offset, leap-second handling (23:59:60), and the '-00:00' convention meaning the UTC instant is known but the local offset is not.

sources.title: RFC 9557 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps with Additional Information
sources.relevance: Time-zone annotations and suffix tags on RFC 3339 timestamps, and the explicit warning that copying a UTC offset into an offset-only time zone wrongly asserts that the offset will never change — grounding the requirement to keep the IANA time zone name alongside the offset.

sources.title: EPCIS Ontology (EPCIS 2.0)
sources.relevance: Machine-readable definition of EPCISEvent and its subclasses (ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, AssociationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent), the eventID/eventTime/eventTimeZoneOffset/recordTime split, action, bizStep, disposition, readPoint, bizLocation, bizTransactionList, sourceList/destinationList, sensorElementList, certificationInfo, and the ErrorDeclaration class with declarationTime, reason and correctiveEventIDs.

sources.title: Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model, version 7.1.3
sources.organization: CIDOC CRM Special Interest Group / ICOM
sources.relevance: Scope notes for E5 Event, E4 Period, E7 Activity, E52 Time-Span, E53 Place and E93 Presence; properties P4 has time-span, P7 took place at, P11 had participant, P14 carried out by, P17 was motivated by, P9 consists of; and the P173–P185 family expressing fuzzy temporal ordering without precise boundaries.

sources.title: FHIR Event Pattern (Release 5)
sources.version_or_date: FHIR Release 5 (R5), version 5.0.0, Standard for Trial-Use
sources.relevance: The normative Event workflow pattern: identifier, basedOn, partOf, status and statusReason, category/code, subject, encounter, occurrence[x], recorded, reported, performer with function and actor, location, reason, relevantHistory; the status vocabulary including not-done and entered-in-error; and the explicit Event-versus-Request boundary.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SSN/SOSA)
sources.relevance: sosa:Observation, Sampling and Actuation as acts that occur; FeatureOfInterest, ObservableProperty, Procedure and Sensor; and the normative distinction between sosa:phenomenonTime (the time the result applies to the feature) and sosa:resultTime (when the act completed).

sources.title: CloudEvents — Version 1.0.2 Specification
sources.organization: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Serverless Working Group
sources.relevance: Definitions of occurrence ('the capture of a statement of fact') versus event ('a data record expressing an occurrence and its context'); REQUIRED attributes id, source, specversion, type; OPTIONAL time, subject, dataschema, datacontenttype; the rule that source+id MUST be unique per distinct event and the duplicate-detection consequence; and the caveat that producers may substitute an alternative time when the true occurrence time is unavailable.

sources.title: Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF) Specification
sources.organization: Library of Congress, Network Development and MARC Standards Office
sources.version_or_date: Specification of 22 October 2018, last modified 4 February 2019; incorporated as a profile of ISO 8601-2:2019
sources.relevance: Level 0/1/2 syntax for reduced precision, uncertain '?', approximate '~', uncertain-and-approximate '%', unspecified digits 'X', open and unknown interval endpoints ('..'), seasons and sub-year groupings, and one-of '[]' versus all-of '{}' sets — the only fetched source giving a normative encoding for temporal uncertainty.

sources.title: OGC GeoSPARQL — A Geographic Query Language for RDF Data, version 1.1
sources.relevance: geo:SpatialObject, geo:Feature and geo:Geometry with hasGeometry, hasDefaultGeometry, hasSerialization, asWKT, asGeoJSON, hasCentroid and hasBoundingBox, and the requirement to declare the coordinate reference system by URI — grounding the separation of place identity from geometric representation.

sources.title: Event — Schema.org Type
sources.relevance: Widely deployed public event typing with startDate/endDate/duration, location including VirtualLocation, eventAttendanceMode, superEvent/subEvent, organizer/performer/attendee, identifier — and the eventStatus vocabulary (EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled) whose scheduling orientation is the counterexample that separates schedule state from factual status.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Policy (Set/Offer/Agreement), Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Asset, Party, Action, Constraint, assigner/assignee roles and the conflict-resolution strategies perm/prohibit/invalid — a machine-readable grounding for participant-level disclosure control and for exceptions expressed as duties.

sources.title: Art. 5 GDPR — Principles relating to processing of personal data (unofficial reproduction of Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
sources.version_or_date: Reproduction of Regulation (EU) 2016/679; page accessed 25 August 2026
sources.relevance: Purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy (inaccurate data erased or rectified without delay) and storage limitation with the Article 89 archiving derogation — used only because the official EUR-Lex text could not be retrieved live at access time.

sources.title: Art. 17 GDPR — Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten') (unofficial reproduction of Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
sources.version_or_date: Reproduction of Regulation (EU) 2016/679; page accessed 25 August 2026
sources.relevance: Grounds for erasure in Article 17(1) and the Article 17(3) exceptions for freedom of expression, legal obligation and public-interest tasks, public health, archiving/scientific/historical research and statistics, and the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims — the exception set that reconciles erasure with an append-only occurrence record.

sources.title: Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model, Version 7.0 and 7.1.3 (ISO 21127:2023 content)
sources.organization: CIDOC CRM Special Interest Group / ICOM
sources.relevance: E5 Event and E7 Activity scope notes, E52 Time-Span inner and outer bounds (P81/P82), participation (P11, P12, P14), meronymy (P9) and influence (P15) that ground the occurrence backbone.

sources.title: ISO 21127:2023 Information and documentation — A reference ontology for the interchange of cultural heritage information
sources.relevance: Formal standard status of the CIDOC CRM alignment target used in the E5 Event alignment entry.

sources.title: schema.org EventStatusType
sources.relevance: Schedule-plane status values EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled and EventMovedOnline, plus previousStartDate.

sources.title: RFC 3339 Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Instant timestamps with seconds and explicit numeric offset or Z, the -00:00 unknown-offset convention, leap-second second=60, and the limits of RFC 3339 for intervals and non-Gregorian calendars.

sources.title: GS1 EPCIS Standard (ISO/IEC 19987) — visibility event data model
sources.relevance: eventTime versus recordTime and eventTimeZoneOffset, ObjectEvent/AggregationEvent/TransactionEvent/TransformationEvent/AssociationEvent, bizStep and disposition, readPoint versus bizLocation, and ADD/OBSERVE/DELETE action.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021 Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) and BFO 2020 occurrent hierarchy
sources.relevance: Occurrent hierarchy in which unfolding happenings are processes and instantaneous beginnings and endings are process boundaries, with no separate Event class.

bundles.name: Occurrence Core
bundles.description: The identity, boundary, type and factual status of the happening itself, before anything is said about time, place, participation or cause.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O, CIDOC CRM, EPCIS, the FHIR Event pattern and CloudEvents all require a typed, identified, individuated occurrence as the anchor for every further assertion; CloudEvents makes identity normative (source+id MUST be unique) and FHIR makes factual status normative (not-done, entered-in-error).

layers.name: Identity and Individuation
layers.description: How one occurrence is delimited from the continuum of activity and how that single occurrence is named and re-found across systems.

findings.name: Occurrence identifier and deduplication key
findings.description: The authoritative name of the occurrence record, the scheme it belongs to, the fallback minting rule when no master system exists, and the key on which two records are judged to denote the same happening.

questions.text: Which system of record holds the authoritative identifier for this occurrence, and under what identifier scheme was it issued?
answer_data: Name and IRI of the master system

questions.text: What combination of attributes decides that two incoming records denote the same occurrence rather than two distinct occurrences?
answer_data: Ordered list of deduplication key elements
Producer context identifier equivalent to a CloudEvents source

questions.text: When no master-system identifier exists, is a governed IRI or a locally minted UUID or ULID used, and which authority mints it?
answer_data: Mint instant in RFC 3339 with offset

questions.text: Under what conditions may the identifier be superseded, and how does a consumer resolve an old identifier to the current record?
answer_data: Resolution endpoint or alias register reference

data_elements.name: occurrenceIdentifier
data_elements.description: The authoritative identifier of the occurrence record.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Scheme or namespace under which the identifier was issued.

data_elements.name: alternateIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifiers assigned by other systems for the same occurrence, including superseded ones.

data_elements.name: deduplicationKey
data_elements.description: Canonical key or digest used to detect that two records denote the same happening.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifier assignment yields no separate deliverable: identifiers are inline attributes of the occurrence record and of any artifact that carries it. Nothing is produced, filed or exchanged as a standalone object, so introducing an artifact here would be unsupported structure.

findings.name: Occurrence boundary and granularity
findings.description: The criterion by which the happening is delimited, whether it is recorded as instantaneous or extended, and what happens when one occurrence is later found to be several or several to be one.

questions.text: What criterion delimits this happening from the surrounding continuum of activity, and who applied it?
Is the occurrence recorded as an instant with no interior or as an extended process with internal constituent parts?
answer_data: Whether constituents are exhaustive of the whole

questions.text: How is the record repaired when one recorded occurrence turns out to be two, or two turn out to be one?
answer_data: References to resulting and retired occurrences
Declaration time and reason for the restructuring

data_elements.name: granularityLevel
data_elements.description: Declared level of resolution at which the happening was individuated.

data_elements.name: isInstantaneous
data_elements.description: Whether the occurrence is asserted to have zero extent at the recorded granularity.

data_elements.name: splitOrMergeLink
data_elements.description: Link from a retired occurrence to the occurrences that replaced it, or from several to the one that subsumed them.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Individuation is a recorded modelling decision expressed as inline attributes and links between occurrence records; no fetched source treats it as producing a filed deliverable, and inventing one would be unsupported.

findings.name: Summary and aboutness
findings.description: An occurrence has a human-readable name or summary and may be about other entities. Schema.org Event requires name and allows description, disambiguatingDescription, about and workFeatured or workPerformed. CIDOC P3 has note and P129 is about. FHIR Event.note captures comments by performer or subject. The summary is not a substitute for structured type, time or participants.

questions.text: What short summary distinguishes this occurrence from similar happenings, and in which language?
Which entities, works or topics is the occurrence about or did it feature, without treating those as participants?
What disambiguating description is required when name and type are insufficient to separate this particular from another of the same kind?

data_elements.name: name
data_elements.description: Human-readable name of the occurrence, as required by schema.org Event.

data_elements.name: summary
data_elements.description: Short summary that distinguishes this occurrence from similar happenings.

data_elements.name: description
data_elements.description: Longer description or note about the happening (schema.org description; CIDOC P3 has note; FHIR Event.note).

data_elements.name: about_refs
data_elements.description: Entities, works or topics the occurrence is about (CIDOC P129 is about; schema.org about, workFeatured, workPerformed), which are not participants.

data_elements.name: language
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag of the name, summary and description text.

artifacts.name: Occurrence narrative
artifacts.description: Language-tagged name, summary and optional notes used to disambiguate the happening.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent occurrence identifier plus BCP 47 language tag.

layers.name: Typing and Factuality
layers.description: What kind of occurrence this is, and whether it is asserted to have happened, to be ongoing, not to have happened, or to have been recorded in error.

findings.name: Occurrence type and governing vocabulary
findings.description: The code or codes classifying the occurrence, the scheme that governs them, who may extend that scheme, and how local types map to external event vocabularies.

questions.text: Which type code or codes classify this occurrence, and from which governed scheme and version do they come?
May an occurrence carry more than one type, and how are conflicting or overlapping types reconciled?
Which body governs the type vocabulary, and what is the procedure for adding or retiring a code value?
To which external event vocabularies is each local type mapped, and is the mapping exact, broader or narrower?

data_elements.name: occurrenceTypeCode
data_elements.description: Code classifying the kind of occurrence.

data_elements.name: typeSchemeUri
data_elements.description: IRI and version of the scheme governing the type code.

data_elements.name: externalTypeMapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from the local type to an external vocabulary term, with the relation kind.

artifacts.name: Occurrence type code list
artifacts.description: The published, versioned code list of occurrence types with scheme IRI, labels, definitions, effective date and mappings to external vocabularies.
media_or_form: controlled vocabulary file (SKOS, CSV or JSON)
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme IRI plus version tag issued by the governing registry; where the list is Dimension-local, a Dimension-minted UUID recorded with its minting authority. The publication date is metadata, never the identifier.

findings.name: Factual assertion and record status
findings.description: Whether the happening is asserted to have occurred, is ongoing, is asserted not to have occurred, or the record is repudiated as entered in error, together with the reason and the allowed transitions.

questions.text: What is the current status of this occurrence record, and does that status describe the happening or the record?
answer_data: Whether the code applies to the happening or the record
Instant at which the status took effect

questions.text: Which status transitions are permitted, which are terminal, and who is authorised to make each transition?
When the record asserts that the happening did not occur, what evidence and reason support that negative assertion?
How is schedule state such as cancelled, postponed or rescheduled kept distinct from the assertion that the happening occurred?

data_elements.name: recordStatus
data_elements.description: Status of the occurrence record drawn from a governed status vocabulary that includes an in-error value.

data_elements.name: statusReason
data_elements.description: Coded reason qualifying the status, required for negative and in-error statuses.

data_elements.name: assertedNotOccurred
data_elements.description: Explicit assertion that the happening did not take place.

data_elements.name: statusEffectiveAt
data_elements.description: Instant at which the current status took effect.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is a coded inline attribute with a transition history; the deliverable that accompanies a repudiation is the correction notice recorded under the correction finding, so duplicating an artifact here would double-count the same object.

bundles.name: Temporality
bundles.description: When the occurrence happened, in what frame that time is expressed, how precisely it is known, and how event time is separated from the times at which it was observed, recorded and corrected.
bundles.rationale: OWL-Time supplies the instant/interval model and the explicit temporal reference system; RFC 3339 and RFC 9557 fix the lexical form and warn against offset-only zones; EPCIS separates eventTime, eventTimeZoneOffset and recordTime; SOSA separates phenomenonTime from resultTime; EDTF supplies the only fetched normative encoding of temporal uncertainty.

layers.name: Temporal Position, Extent and Uncertainty
layers.description: The stated time of the happening as instant, interval or duration, the reference frame it is expressed in, and the precision and qualification attached to it.

findings.name: Event time position and extent
findings.description: Whether the occurrence is placed at an instant or over an interval, how beginning, end and duration are stated, and how open-ended or still-running occurrences are expressed.

questions.text: Is the event time expressed as an instant, a bounded interval, or a duration anchored at one end?
How is an occurrence that has begun but not ended, or whose end is unknown, distinguished from one with a known end?
answer_data: Latest instant at which the occurrence was known to be running

questions.text: Where the boundaries are inherently fuzzy, which outer and inner bounds are asserted for the beginning and the end?

data_elements.name: eventTimeBegin
data_elements.description: Instant at which the occurrence began, or the instant of an instantaneous occurrence.

data_elements.name: eventTimeEnd
data_elements.description: Instant at which the occurrence ended, absent for open-ended or instantaneous occurrences.

data_elements.name: eventDuration
data_elements.description: Extent of the occurrence expressed as a duration with a stated temporal unit.

data_elements.name: temporalOuterBounds
data_elements.description: Asserted earliest and latest possible boundary instants where the true boundary is fuzzy.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal position is inline value data typed by OWL-Time and serialised as timestamp literals; no fetched source treats a time statement as a separate filed object.

findings.name: Temporal reference frame, offset and time zone
findings.description: The calendar or temporal reference system in which the time is expressed, the required lexical form, and the retention of local offset and IANA time zone name alongside the UTC instant.

questions.text: Which temporal reference system is the event time expressed in, and is it declared explicitly rather than assumed to be Gregorian and UTC?
answer_data: Whether the frame is declared or defaulted

questions.text: What UTC offset was in effect at the place of the occurrence, and is the IANA time zone name recorded in addition to that offset?
answer_data: Whether '-00:00' was used to mean the local offset is unknown

questions.text: How are ordinal, relative, geologic or non-Gregorian times conveyed to consumers that expect a civil timestamp?
answer_data: Conversion rule or refusal to convert
Consumer guidance recorded with the value

data_elements.name: eventTimeZoneOffset
data_elements.description: UTC offset in effect where the occurrence took place, kept as a separate element from the normalised instant.

data_elements.name: timeZoneName
data_elements.description: IANA time zone name for the place of the occurrence.

data_elements.name: temporalReferenceSystem
data_elements.description: IRI of the temporal reference system when it is not the Gregorian calendar with UTC.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The reference frame is a declared attribute of a time value; the only candidate artifact — a time-source attestation — is recorded under ordering and clock integrity to avoid duplicating the same deliverable.

findings.name: Temporal precision, approximation and uncertainty
findings.description: The stated precision of the time value and any qualification marking it uncertain, approximate, partly unspecified or drawn from a set of alternatives.

questions.text: To what precision is the event time actually known, as distinct from the precision at which it happens to be serialised?
Is the time asserted as uncertain, approximate, both, or partly unspecified, and to which components does the qualification apply?
How must a consumer treat an imprecise or qualified time value when ordering, filtering or joining occurrences?
answer_data: Behaviour when precision differs between operands
Whether qualified values may be silently coerced

data_elements.name: statedTimePrecision
data_elements.description: Unit to which the event time is genuinely known.

data_elements.name: temporalQualification
data_elements.description: Uncertainty or approximation marker attached to the time value or to specific components of it.

data_elements.name: qualifiedDateLiteral
data_elements.description: The qualified date expression exactly as written, preserved verbatim because its characters are semantically significant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Uncertainty qualification is a literal syntax carried inside the time value itself; it has no independent existence as a deliverable and must not be normalised away into a separate object.

layers.name: Record Time, Observation Time and Ordering
layers.description: The distinct clocks that bear on an occurrence record — when it happened, when it was observed, when the result applies, when it was ingested, when a correction was declared — and how records are ordered when those clocks disagree.

findings.name: Event time versus observation and ingestion time
findings.description: Separation of the time the happening occurred from the time a result applies to its subject, the time the observing act completed, the time the record entered the store, and the time any correction was declared.

questions.text: Which distinct times are recorded for this occurrence, and which clock produced each of them?
answer_data: Clock or system responsible for each

questions.text: Where the record carries an observation, does the phenomenon time differ from the time the observing act completed, and by how much?
Which of the recorded times governs retention clocks, query windows and completeness watermarks?
answer_data: Behaviour when the governing time is absent

questions.text: How is a record ingested long after the fact distinguished from one captured in near real time?
answer_data: Latency between event time and record time
Reporting party for the late record

data_elements.name: recordTime
data_elements.description: Instant at which the occurrence record was accepted into the store.

data_elements.name: resultTime
data_elements.description: Instant at which an observing, sampling or actuating act that produced the record completed.

data_elements.name: phenomenonTime
data_elements.description: Time to which an observed result applies to its feature of interest, which may precede the result time.

data_elements.name: declarationTime
data_elements.description: Instant at which an error declaration or other assertion about the record was made.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are parallel timestamp attributes of one record; the artifact that carries them is the occurrence record itself, which is exchanged under the delivery finding rather than filed separately here.

findings.name: Ordering, interval relations and clock integrity
findings.description: How occurrences are ordered when timestamps tie or clocks disagree, which qualitative interval relations are asserted, and what evidence supports the trustworthiness of the recorded time.

questions.text: When two occurrences carry the same timestamp, what deterministic rule establishes their order?
answer_data: Scope within which the sequence is unique

questions.text: Which qualitative interval relations between this occurrence and others are asserted rather than computed from timestamps?
What is known about the clock that produced the timestamp, and what protects the record against back-dating?
answer_data: Offset or drift applied at capture
Attestation or signature covering the timestamp

data_elements.name: sequenceNumber
data_elements.description: Monotonic counter establishing order within a declared scope when timestamps are insufficient.

data_elements.name: assertedIntervalRelation
data_elements.description: Qualitative temporal relation asserted between this occurrence and another.

data_elements.name: clockSource
data_elements.description: Identity and synchronisation state of the clock that produced the recorded time.

artifacts.name: Time source attestation
artifacts.description: Record of the clock source, its synchronisation status and any offset applied at the moment the occurrence timestamp was captured, used when the trustworthiness of the time itself is in question.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier of the capturing device or gateway plus the attestation instant expressed in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; where no device identifier exists, a Dimension-minted UUID with recorded minting authority.

bundles.name: Spatiality and Setting
bundles.description: Where the occurrence took place — as a reference to an identified place, as geometry in a declared reference system, or as a non-physical setting — and at what granularity and accuracy.
bundles.rationale: CIDOC P7 took place at, PROV atLocation and EPCIS readPoint/bizLocation all make a place statement part of an occurrence, while GeoSPARQL supplies the normative separation of Feature identity from Geometry and the requirement to declare a CRS; schema.org adds VirtualLocation and attendance mode for non-physical settings.

layers.name: Place Specification
layers.description: The reference to where the occurrence happened and its geometric expression, kept distinct from the identity of the place itself.

findings.name: Place reference, role and granularity
findings.description: Which identified place the occurrence is attached to, in what role that place plays, at what granularity, and how an unknown or deliberately withheld place is expressed.

questions.text: Which identified place does this occurrence reference, and in which external register does that identity live?
answer_data: Place feature IRI or master-system identifier

questions.text: Does the record distinguish the precise point of capture from the wider business or organisational location, and how are both used?
At what granularity is the place asserted, and is that granularity a limit of knowledge or a deliberate generalisation?
How is a place that is unknown, inapplicable or withheld distinguished from one that was simply not captured?

data_elements.name: placeReference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally identified place at which the occurrence took place.

data_elements.name: capturePointReference
data_elements.description: The precise point at which the occurrence was captured, as distinct from the enclosing location.

data_elements.name: placeGranularity
data_elements.description: Declared level of spatial resolution of the place statement.

data_elements.name: placeAbsenceReason
data_elements.description: Coded reason why no place is asserted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A place statement is a typed reference into the Address / Location Referencing model; the referenced place record is that model's artifact, and duplicating it here would violate the no-duplication boundary rule.

findings.name: Geometry, coordinate reference system and positional accuracy
findings.description: The geometric representation of where the occurrence happened, the coordinate reference system it is expressed in, its positional accuracy, and any generalisation applied before disclosure.

questions.text: In which serialisation is the geometry expressed, and which coordinate reference system URI governs its coordinates?
answer_data: Whether a default CRS was assumed

questions.text: What positional accuracy is claimed for the geometry, and what produced that claim?

Merged alternate identifiers and corroborating sources
New conflicting-account link where the accounts disagree
preconditions: The deduplication key is declared for the occurrence type
Producer context is available for identifier scoping
effects: Redeliveries do not create spurious occurrences
Genuinely independent accounts are retained rather than collapsed

functions.name: Assert a causal or influence link
functions.description: Record an asserted influence between two occurrences with its kind, asserter, basis and confidence, subject to temporal and acyclicity constraints.
outputs: Persisted influence link
Constraint violation report where the link is cyclic or temporally impossible
Updated causal graph view
preconditions: Both occurrences exist and carry event times or explicit ordering
An asserter is identified; the link is never inferred from order alone
effects: The causal graph gains an attributable, falsifiable edge
Downstream explanations can cite the asserter rather than the system

functions.name: Compose an aggregate or episode
functions.description: Group related occurrences into a larger occurrence, episode or series instance and derive or assert the aggregate's temporal span.
inputs: Span derivation rule or asserted span
outputs: Aggregate occurrence with membership links
Derived or asserted aggregate span
Recomputation record when membership changes
preconditions: Members exist and the grouping criterion is stated
Multiple-membership policy is configured
effects: Members become navigable from the whole and vice versa
Span changes propagate deterministically when membership changes

functions.name: Declare error and issue correction
functions.description: Repudiate an erroneous occurrence record without mutating it and file the corrective records that supersede it.
outputs: Correction notice with declaration time and reason
Corrective occurrence records linked to the erroneous one
In-error marker on the original, which retains its identifier and content
preconditions: The declaring party is authorised to repudiate
The change is material rather than additive
effects: History is preserved and the error itself becomes part of the record
Consumers holding the original can detect supersession

functions.name: Project and disclose
functions.description: Produce a named projection of an occurrence for a stated audience, applying the access policy, participant grants and any spatial or personal generalisation.
inputs: Applicable access policies and participant grants
outputs: Projection containing only permitted elements
Omission profile stating what was withheld and why
Access audit entry
preconditions: A visibility class and at least one applicable policy exist
Conflicts between policies resolve under a declared strategy
effects: Non-consenting participation is omitted rather than obscured
Every disclosure is auditable against its policy basis

Disposition certificate

Exceptions have been evaluated before any destructive action

Every disposition leaves auditable evidence of what was done and why

Conformance is claimed only where evidenced

Conflict flags are carried with the mapping
